summary: Follow-up of the accepted BSD.7 packet for stage BSD.9, reading its remaining work under the maintainer's 2026-10-16 decision that explicit curve data are hypotheses and computations are not targets. It plans the four public endpoints (rank equality, finite Ш, the p-part as a named proposition PrimePartFormula, and the full formula from a complete certificate) and proves that the roadmap's L-function, rank and quotient meet the statement-only BSD milestone of EllipticCurves Layer 7. On the analytic side it plans the coefficient bound |a_n| ≤ σ₀(n)√n, series and inequalities for the exponential integral (on QSeries QM.3's incomplete gamma), an explicit nonvanishing criterion turning a finite-sum inequality into analytic rank 0 or 1, Manin's closing-the-path formula with the denominator 2(1 + p − a_p), and the exact rank-zero quotient from a denominator and an enclosure. On the arithmetic side it checks the named branches' side conditions in general (rational p-torsion forces an ordinary Eisenstein prime outside CGS but inside Keller–Yin; CM curves meet no BSD.6 branch; no branch reaches p = 2) and proves odd-primary Ш vanishing from a Heegner index, with Gross's X₀(37)/w₃₇ example. Applications to 11a3, 37a1 and 32a2 take all numerical and descent data as hypotheses.

nodes.title: The p-part of the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer formula
nodes.statement: For an elliptic curve E/ℚ with h : analyticRank E ≤ 1 and a natural prime p, PrimePartFormula E h p is the proposition padicValRat p (bsdDefect E) = 0, where bsdDefect E ∈ ℚ_{>0} is the rational BSD defect of BSD.5 (leading term times #E(ℚ)_tors² divided by Ω_E·Reg_BSD(E/ℚ)·#Ш(E/ℚ)·∏_ℓ c_ℓ(E)). Unfolded, it says v_p(L*/(Ω_E Reg_BSD)) = v_p(∏_ℓ c_ℓ(E)) + v_p(#Ш(E/ℚ)) − 2·v_p(#E(ℚ)_tors), where L*/(Ω_E Reg_BSD) is the positive rational number of BSD.5 and L* = leadingTerm E. It concerns one prime only: it is not the full formula, and at p = 2 it depends on using Reg_BSD (the x-height normalisation) rather than the pinned halved regulator.
hypotheses: E/ℚ is elliptic and analyticRank E ≤ 1, so that bsdDefect E is defined and Ш(E/ℚ) is finite (BSD.4).
p is a natural prime; the regulator is GZ.0's Reg_BSD and the period is the full real Néron period.
proofSteps: Define the proposition by the valuation of BSD.5's bsdDefect; no new arithmetic object is introduced.

Unfold with padicValRat.mul, padicValRat.div and padicValRat.pow, using that every factor of the defect is a nonzero rational (positivity from BSD.5/leading-term-positivity, finiteness from BSD.4); this gives the valuation identity and its equivalence with the printed form of Keller–Yin Theorem C and CGS Theorem D, since v_p(#Ш(E/ℚ)) = v_p(#Ш(E/ℚ)[p^∞]).
Isogeny invariance: BSD.5/defect-isogeny-invariance gives equal defects for ℚ-isogenous curves.
Full formula: positive-rational-reconstruction (BSD.8) gives (∀ p prime, PrimePartFormula E h p) ↔ bsdDefect E = 1.
acceptance: The torsion order enters squared: a definition with #E(ℚ)_tors to the first power fails the 11a3 data check.
The statement at all odd primes does not imply the statement at 2 (dyadic-gate countermodels).

nodes.title: The roadmap's L-function, rank and quotient against the EllipticCurves BSD statement
nodes.statement: Let E/ℚ be elliptic. (i) ellipticL E is entire and equals E.LSeries on Re s > 3/2, so it is an admissible analytic hypothesis of the statement-only Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer milestone of EllipticCurves Layer 7 (an analytic function on a connected open set containing s = 1 and part of the half-plane of convergence, agreeing with the actual Dirichlet series there). (ii) Every admissible continuation G on a connected open set U equals ellipticL E on U, so the order of vanishing and the leading coefficient L^{(r)}(1)/r! of that statement are analyticRank E and leadingTerm E. (iii) If analyticRank E ≤ 1, BSD.4 discharges the statement's finiteness hypothesis on Ш(E/ℚ); the statement's quotient Ω(E)·Reg(E/ℚ)·#Ш·∏_p c_p/#E(ℚ)_tors², with Layer 7's explicit-integral period and Layer 6's x-height regulator, is the denominator Ω_E·Reg_BSD·#Ш·∏c_ℓ/#tors² of BSD.5's defect. Hence the statement's rank equality holds for E, and its leading-coefficient identity holds if and only if bsdDefect E = 1.
hypotheses: E/ℚ elliptic; (iii) assumes analyticRank E ≤ 1.

Normalisation: Layer 6 of current EllipticCurves fixes ĥ(P) = lim h(x(nP))/n², whose regulator is Reg_BSD. At the Tau Ceti pin f790474 the canonical height is half of that; a statement instantiated with the pinned regulator differs by the factor 2^r (GZ.0/height-convention-dictionary).
proofSteps: (i) BSD.0/actual-l-function: entire, and equal to E.LSeries for Re s > 3/2; that half-plane lies in the half-plane of absolute convergence, and ℂ is connected.

(ii) On its half-plane of convergence the Dirichlet series is analytic and, by the identity theorem from Re s > 3/2, equals ellipticL E there. G agrees with the series on a nonempty open subset of U, so Mathlib's AnalyticOnNhd.eqOn_of_preconnected_of_eventuallyEq gives G = ellipticL E on U; orders at 1 and iterated derivatives at 1 coincide.

(iii) BSD.4/analytic-rank-at-most-one-theorem gives finiteness and the rank equality; GZ.0/real-period-components identifies Layer 7's integral 2∫_{D_W>0}dx/√D_W with the full Néron period; GZ.0/bsd-regulator identifies the x-height regulator with Reg_BSD; compare with the definition of bsdDefect.
acceptance: An arbitrary analytic germ at s = 1 is not admissible: two germs can differ while only ellipticL E agrees with the Dirichlet series.
Counting c∞ again on top of Layer 7's period would divide the quotient by 2 on curves with Δ > 0.

nodes.title: Public endpoint: the formula at one prime
nodes.statement: Let E/ℚ be elliptic with h : analyticRank E ≤ 1 and p prime. Each of the following, with exactly the hypotheses of its node, proves PrimePartFormula E h p: the rank-zero ordinary/multiplicative branch, the rank-zero supersingular branch, the Jetchev–Skinner–Wan rank-one branch, Castella's Theorem A′ and the BSTW rank-one branch (BSD.6), the Castella–Grossi–Skinner and Keller–Yin good Eisenstein branches (BSD.7), and an exceptional-prime computation of v_p(bsdDefect E) (BSD.8). There is one public declaration per branch; no public signature takes a disjunction of branches whose hypotheses could be discharged by an unproved claim that p is good, large or irreducible.
hypotheses: E/ℚ elliptic, analyticRank E ≤ 1, p prime, plus the full hypothesis list of the chosen branch.
proofSteps: For each branch, compose its conclusion v_p(bsdDefect E) = 0 with the definition of PrimePartFormula.
The dispatch BSD.8/source-qualified-prime-part-dispatch already proves the conclusion branch by branch; this node fixes the public names and signatures.
acceptance: At p = 2 none of the seven named branches applies (dyadic-branch-exclusion).
On curves with rational p-torsion at a good odd p only the Keller–Yin branch applies at p (rational-torsion-eisenstein-ordinary).

sources.match: A fixed-prime leading-term formula is a separate public signature, and each source's side conditions are proved before its theorem is applied.

nodes.title: Public endpoint: the full leading-term formula from a complete certificate
nodes.statement: Let E/ℚ be elliptic with h : analyticRank E ≤ 1, and let c be a Rat.PrimeValuationCertificate for bsdDefect E. Then both conclusions of EllipticCurves Layer 7's BSD statement hold for E: the rank equality and the identity leadingTerm E = Ω_E·Reg_BSD(E/ℚ)·#Ш(E/ℚ)·∏_ℓ c_ℓ(E)/#E(ℚ)_tors². Equivalently PrimePartFormula E h p for every prime p.
hypotheses: E/ℚ elliptic, analyticRank E ≤ 1, a complete finite certificate for the actual defect.
proofSteps: BSD.8/elliptic-endpoint gives the real identity; ec-bsd-statement-compatibility (iii) identifies it with Layer 7's leading-coefficient identity; public-rank-endpoint gives the other conclusion.
BSD.8/certificate-all-primes gives v_p(bsdDefect E) = 0 at every prime, i.e. the equivalent form.
acceptance: The rank and Ш endpoints do not consume this one; deleting the certificate's dyadic entry blocks only this endpoint (missing-exception-fixture).
With supplied data giving bsdDefect E = 1 exactly, the canonical certificate ofAllPrimes applies (conditional-full-formula).

nodes.title: Coefficient bound for the L-series of an elliptic curve
nodes.statement: For E/ℚ elliptic and every n ≥ 1, the coefficient a_n = E.LFunction n of Mathlib's formal Euler product satisfies |a_n| ≤ σ₀(n)·√n, where σ₀(n) is the number of divisors of n. Since σ₀(n) ≤ 2√n, also |a_n| ≤ 2n.
hypotheses: E/ℚ elliptic; a_n is Mathlib's coefficient, defined through the minimal model and its reductions.
proofSteps: The Euler product makes n ↦ a_n multiplicative, and σ₀ is multiplicative (Nat.Coprime.card_divisors_mul).

Good p: the local factor is 1 − a_pT + pT²; with the roots α, β of X² − a_pX + p one has a_{p^k} = Σ_{i=0}^k α^iβ^{k−i}, and the Hasse bound |a_p| ≤ 2√p (EllipticCurves Layer 3) gives |α| = |β| = √p, so |a_{p^k}| ≤ (k+1)p^{k/2} = σ₀(p^k)p^{k/2} (ArithmeticFunction.sigma_zero_apply_prime_pow).
Bad p: the local factor is 1 − T, 1 + T or 1, so a_{p^k} = a_p^k with a_p ∈ {1, −1, 0} and |a_{p^k}| ≤ 1.
Multiply over the prime powers of n. For σ₀(n) ≤ 2√n pair each divisor d ≤ √n with n/d.
acceptance: Equality |a_p| = σ₀(p)√p is impossible for an integer a_p and p prime; the bound is attained only up to the Hasse slack (e.g. a_2 = −2 for 37a1, where 2√2 ≈ 2.83).
The weaker |a_n| ≤ √n fails: a_2 = −2 for 11a3.

sources.match: The local polynomial is 1 − aT + qT² at good reduction and 1 − T, 1 + T, 1 at split, nonsplit and additive reduction; the L-function is the Euler product of their inverses.
The Dirichlet series of a rational newform has the Euler product with good and bad factors of this shape.
σ₀(p^i) = i + 1 and σ₀ is multiplicative.

nodes.title: Series and inequalities for the exponential integral
nodes.statement: For x > 0 let E₁(x) = Γ(0, x) = ∫_x^∞ e^{−t}t^{−1} dt, the upper incomplete gamma function of QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.3 at s = 0. Then: (i) E₁(x) = −γ − log x + Σ_{n≥1} (−1)^{n+1}x^n/(n·n!), the series converging absolutely, with γ Euler's constant; (ii) for K ≥ x the terms x^n/(n·n!) decrease for n ≥ K, so truncating the series after any n ≥ K errs by at most the first omitted term; (iii) x/(x+1) < x·e^x·E₁(x) < (x+1)/(x+2) and ½·log(1+2/x) < e^x E₁(x) < log(1+1/x); in particular e^{−x}/(x+1) < E₁(x) < e^{−x}/x; (iv) E₁ is positive and strictly decreasing on (0, ∞). With Mathlib's bounds 1/2 < γ < 2/3 and its monotone sequences converging to γ, (i)–(iii) bound E₁ at a positive real argument between explicit elementary expressions.
hypotheses: x > 0 real. The function is QM.3's Γ(0, ·); no second exponential-integral carrier is introduced.
proofSteps: (i) Put Ein(x) = Σ_{n≥1}(−1)^{n+1}x^n/(n·n!) = ∫_0^x (1 − e^{−t})t^{−1}dt (termwise integration). The function E₁(x) + log x − Ein(x) has derivative zero on (0, ∞), and its limit at 0⁺ is −γ by the integral representation of γ (Mathlib's eulerMascheroniConstant via the derivative of Γ at 1, Real.eulerMascheroniConstant_eq_neg_deriv).
(ii) The ratio of consecutive terms is x·n/((n+1)²) ≤ x/(n+1) < 1 once n + 1 > x; apply the alternating-series estimate.

(iii) e^x E₁(x) = ∫_0^∞ e^{−u}/(x+u) du; Jensen's inequality for the convex u ↦ 1/(x+u) against the probability density e^{−u} gives the lower bound 1/(x+1); the remaining two-sided bounds are DLMF 6.8.1–6.8.3.
(iv) The integrand is positive and the derivative is −e^{−x}/x < 0.
acceptance: At x = 1: the bounds give 0.1839 < E₁(1) < 0.2707 (from (iii), first form), consistent with E₁(1) = 0.21938…
Dropping the minus sign in front of γ in (i) changes E₁(x) by 2γ > 1 and violates (iii) at x = 1.

sources.match: The power series of E₁ about 0, with the −γ − ln z leading terms.
Two-sided bounds for e^x E₁(x) and x e^x E₁(x) for real x > 0.
G₁(x) is the exponential integral, evaluated by this series for small x and a continued fraction for large x.
Explicit bounds on γ.

nodes.title: Explicit nonvanishing criterion for L(E,1) and L′(E,1)
nodes.statement: Let E/ℚ be elliptic of conductor N, β = 2π/√N, ρ = e^{−β}, a_n = E.LFunction n and M ≥ 1. Put S₀(M) = 2Σ_{n≤M}(a_n/n)e^{−βn}, S₁(M) = 2Σ_{n≤M}(a_n/n)E₁(βn), T₀(M) = 4ρ^{M+1}/(1−ρ) and T₁(M) = 4ρ^{M+1}/(β(M+1)(1−ρ)). (i) If rootNumber E = 1 then |ellipticL E 1 − S₀(M)| ≤ T₀(M); if moreover |S₀(M)| > T₀(M), then analyticRank E = 0 and leadingTerm E lies in [S₀(M) − T₀(M), S₀(M) + T₀(M)]. (ii) If rootNumber E = −1 then ellipticL E 1 = 0 and |deriv (ellipticL E) 1 − S₁(M)| ≤ T₁(M); if moreover |S₁(M)| > T₁(M), then analyticRank E = 1 and leadingTerm E lies in [S₁(M) − T₁(M), S₁(M) + T₁(M)]. (iii) An inequality |S| + T < δ bounds the value by δ and never proves vanishing. The theorem contains no computation: its hypothesis is an inequality between explicit real numbers, which outward rational bounds on e^{−βn} and on E₁(βn) (exponential-integral-bounds) reduce to finitely many rational inequalities.
hypotheses: E/ℚ elliptic; N its conductor (the level of F_E, R29.4/exact-conductor); rootNumber E the sign of BSD.0's functional equation; M ≥ 1.
proofSteps: Mellin expressions: BSD.9/mellin-central-tail-bounds (Cremona Propositions 2.11.1 and 2.13.1) gives L(E,1) = 2Σ_{n≥1}(a_n/n)e^{−βn} when the sign is +1 and L′(E,1) = 2Σ_{n≥1}(a_n/n)E₁(βn) when it is −1; BSD.0/root-number-parity gives L(E,1) = 0 in the second case.

Tails: by coefficient-bound |a_n/n| ≤ 2, so the value tail is at most 2Σ_{n>M}2ρ^n = 4ρ^{M+1}/(1−ρ); by exponential-integral-bounds E₁(βn) < e^{−βn}/(βn) ≤ ρ^n/(β(M+1)) for n > M, so the derivative tail is at most 4ρ^{M+1}/(β(M+1)(1−ρ)).

If |S| > T, the true value lies in [S − T, S + T], which excludes 0; BSD.0's analyticRank_eq_zero_iff and analyticRank_eq_one_iff give the order, and leadingTerm E is the value or the first derivative.
acceptance: Diagnostic values (not proofs) with M = 5 and a_n from point counts: conductor 11 (11a3, sign +1): S₀ ≈ 0.25384, T₀ ≈ 5.4·10⁻⁵; conductor 37 (37a1, sign −1): S₁ ≈ 0.30544, T₁ ≈ 2.0·10⁻³; conductor 32 (32a2, sign +1): S₀ ≈ 0.65554, T₀ ≈ 7.6·10⁻³. The hypothesis |S| > T holds in each case with a wide margin.
Using the value formula when the sign is −1 is not licensed: the theorem has no conclusion there, and L(E,1) = 0 comes from the sign alone.

sources.match: The value series when the Fricke eigenvalue gives sign +1, and the r-th derivative series with G_r; G₁ is the exponential integral.
Cremona notes that a sufficiently precise evaluation decides r = 1 when L(f,1) = 0, while no approximation by itself proves vanishing.
Rigorous tails and approximation bounds, then a certified nonzero enclosure; numerical evidence is not a proof.

nodes.title: Manin's closing-the-path formula for L(E,1)/Ω
nodes.statement: Let E/ℚ be elliptic of conductor N with newform F_E = Σ a_n qⁿ, ω_f = 2πi F_E(z)dz, Λ_f ⊂ ℂ the lattice of periods of ω_f over H₁(X₀(N),ℤ), Ω₀ its least positive real element and Ω(f) = 2Ω₀ if Λ_f is rectangular and Ω₀ otherwise. Then: (i) L(E,1) = ⟨{0,∞}, ω_f⟩, the integral of ω_f along the imaginary axis; (ii) for every prime p ∤ N, (1 + p − a_p)·L(E,1) = Σ_{k=0}^{p−1}⟨{0, k/p}, ω_f⟩, where each {0, k/p} is a closed cycle on X₀(N), so the right side is a real element of Λ_f; (iii) 1 + p − a_p > 0 by the Hasse bound. Consequently L(E,1)/Ω(f) ∈ (1/(2(1 + p − a_p)))·ℤ for every p ∤ N, and L(E,1)/Ω(f) ∈ (1/D)·ℤ with D = 2·gcd_{p∈S}(1 + p − a_p) for any finite nonempty set S of primes not dividing N.
hypotheses: E/ℚ elliptic; p prime with p ∤ N. Ω(f) is the period of the newform, not of E: the two are compared through the Manin constant (exact-rank-zero-quotient).
proofSteps: (i) Mellin transform at s = 1: the twisted Mellin formula of ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L1 with trivial character and j = 0, together with R29.6/l-function-continuation (L(E,s) = L(F_E,s)).

(ii) The Hecke operator T_p on modular symbols (L0/hecke-operators) sends {0,∞} to (1 + p){0,∞} minus the sum of the {0, k/p}; integrating ω_f, which is a T_p-eigendifferential with eigenvalue a_p, gives the identity. For p ∤ N the cusps k/p are Γ₀(N)-equivalent to 0, so each path closes up and its period lies in Λ_f (L0/period-symbol).
Reality: the involution at infinity (L0/involution-at-infinity) sends {0, k/p} to {0, (p−k)/p} and the period to its complex conjugate, so the sum is real; Λ_f ∩ ℝ = ℤΩ₀ and Ω(f) ∈ {Ω₀, 2Ω₀}.
(iii) a_p = a_p(E) at p ∤ N (R29.4/bad-euler-factors) and |a_p| ≤ 2√p < p + 1.
acceptance: For 11a1 and p = 2: a_2 = −2, so 1 + p − a_p = 5 and L(E,1)/Ω(f) ∈ (1/10)ℤ; the value is 1/5.
For conductor 32 and p = 3: a_3 = 0, so L(E,1)/Ω(f) ∈ (1/8)ℤ.

sources.match: L(f,1) is the period of the modular symbol {0,∞}; applying T_p and integrating gives (1 + p − a_p)L(f,1) as a sum of integral real periods, whence L(f,1)/Ω(f) = n/(2(1 + p − a_p)) with n an integer.
A modular-symbol expression for the actual central value.

nodes.title: An exact value of L(E,1)/Ω_E from a denominator and an enclosure
nodes.statement: Let E/ℚ be elliptic of conductor N, φ: X₀(N) → E an optimal modular parametrisation with Manin constant c_φ (φ*ω_E = c_φ·ω_f), and S a finite nonempty set of primes not dividing N; put D = 2|c_φ|·gcd_{p∈S}(1 + p − a_p). Then Ω_E = |c_φ|·Ω(f) and L(E,1)/Ω_E ∈ (1/D)·ℤ. Hence, if rationals a < b satisfy b − a ≤ 1/D and a < L(E,1)/Ω_E < b, then L(E,1)/Ω_E is the unique element of (1/D)ℤ in the open interval (a, b). For a curve E′ that is ℚ-isogenous to E, L(E′,1) = L(E,1), and L(E′,1)/Ω_{E′} is obtained from L(E,1)/Ω_E by the rational period ratio Ω_E/Ω_{E′}.
hypotheses: φ optimal (φ_* : H₁(X₀(N),ℤ) → H₁(E(ℂ),ℤ) surjective); c_φ the Manin constant of GZ.3; Ω_E the full real Néron period.
For E′ the period ratio is a supplied comparison (BSD.8/local-isogeny-certificate-adapter, BSD.9/fixture-11-isogeny-period), not deduced from the isogeny degree alone.
proofSteps: Optimality gives Λ_E = c_φ·Λ_f for the period lattice of the Néron differential, so the rectangularity and the least real periods correspond and Ω_E = |c_φ|·Ω(f) (GZ.0/real-period-components for the full period).
Apply manin-closing-the-path for each p ∈ S and take the gcd.
Two distinct elements of (1/D)ℤ differ by at least 1/D ≥ b − a, so at most one lies in (a, b).
Isogenous curves have the same L-function (BSD.0 ellipticL_eq_of_isogenous).
acceptance: For 11a1 (optimal; c_φ = 1) and S = {2}: D = 10, and any enclosure of width at most 1/10 around 0.2 gives L(11a1,1)/Ω = 1/5. With Ω(11a3) = 5Ω(11a1) this gives L(11a3,1)/Ω(11a3) = 1/25.
Without the Manin constant the denominator can be wrong by c_φ: the theorem does not apply to a non-optimal parametrisation without its own index.

sources.locator: §2.8, (2.8.10), p.31, and the discussion following it
sources.match: For the optimal curve the rational number L(f,1)/Ω(f) has the displayed denominator; the curve's own period differs by the Manin constant.
Rationality with an explicit denominator turns an enclosure into an exact value.

nodes.title: Rational p-torsion at a good odd prime
nodes.statement: Let E/ℚ be elliptic, p an odd prime of good reduction and P ∈ E(ℚ) of order p. Then: (i) reduction modulo p is injective on E(ℚ)[p], so p divides #Ẽ(𝔽_p) = p + 1 − a_p, hence a_p ≡ 1 (mod p) and E is ordinary at p; (ii) ⟨P⟩ is the kernel of a cyclic ℚ-rational p-isogeny with trivial kernel character, and by the Weil pairing E[p]^ss ≅ 𝔽_p ⊕ 𝔽_p(ω), so E[p] is reducible and p is an Eisenstein prime; (iii) every cyclic ℚ-rational p-isogeny of E has kernel character 1 or ω (a kernel other than ⟨P⟩ is a complement of ⟨P⟩, isomorphic to μ_p), so the hypothesis φ|G_p ≠ 1, ω of BSD.7/cgs-eisenstein-prime-bsd fails for every choice; (iv) the hypotheses of BSD.7/ky-eisenstein-prime-bsd hold whenever analyticRank E ≤ 1, while no BSD.6 branch applies at p: the irreducible-residual branches fail by (ii), the supersingular ones by (i), and Castella's needs multiplicative reduction at p.
hypotheses: E/ℚ elliptic, p odd prime, E has good reduction at p, P ∈ E(ℚ) of exact order p.
proofSteps: (i) The reduction-injectivity theorem of EllipticCurves Layer 6 (torsion injects at good odd p); then a_p = p + 1 − #Ẽ(𝔽_p) ≡ 1 mod p, and a_p ≢ 0 mod p means ordinary.

(ii) EllipticCurves Layer 1 constructs the isogeny with kernel ⟨P⟩; the Galois group acts trivially on the rational points; the Weil pairing (Layer 2) has determinant ω, so the quotient character is ω.
(iii) If C ≠ ⟨P⟩ is another rational cyclic subgroup, E[p] = ⟨P⟩ ⊕ C and C ≅ E[p]/⟨P⟩ has character ω.
(iv) Compare with the hypothesis lists of the BSD.6 and BSD.7 nodes.
acceptance: 11a3 and p = 5: a_5 = 1 ≡ 1 mod 5 and #Ẽ(𝔽_5) = 5; Keller–Yin applies, CGS does not.
Keller–Yin §0.3 lists the smallest examples 19a3 (p = 3), 11a3 (p = 5) and 26b2 (p = 7).

sources.match: Theorem C needs only a good prime p > 2 and a cyclic p-isogeny; the examples have rational p-torsion and lie outside the earlier local hypothesis.

sources.locator: Theorem A, p.2, and Theorem D, pp.4–5
sources.match: The isogeny character must satisfy φ|G_p ≠ 1, ω, which rational p-torsion violates.
Torsion injects into the reduction at a good odd prime.

nodes.title: Which named branches can apply to a CM curve
nodes.statement: Let E/ℚ be elliptic with complex multiplication (End_ℚ̄(E) ≠ ℤ). Then j(E) ∈ ℤ, E has potentially good reduction at every prime and multiplicative reduction at none, and E has at least one prime of bad reduction, which is therefore additive; so E is not semistable, and no quadratic twist of E is semistable. Consequently, at every prime p, none of the five BSD.6 branches applies to E (each needs semistability, a twist of a semistable curve, or a multiplicative prime), and the BSD.7 branches apply only at good odd primes p where E has a rational p-isogeny. For 32a2 (y² = x³ − x, CM by ℤ[i], additive at 2), whose ℚ-isogeny class has only isogenies of 2-power degree, no named branch applies at any prime: its full formula can only come from an exact computation of the whole defect.
hypotheses: E/ℚ elliptic with CM. The statement about 32a2 additionally uses its isogeny class, a supplied datum.
proofSteps: CM j-invariants are algebraic integers (CM.3/integrality), hence in ℤ for E/ℚ; v_p(j) ≥ 0 at every p is potential good reduction (CM.5/cm-reduction-dictionary; EllipticCurves Layer 4), which excludes multiplicative reduction.

A bad prime exists: by R29.3/R29.4 the newform F_E has level N equal to the conductor; if N = 1 then F_E would be a nonzero weight-2 form of level one, contradicting Mathlib's ModularForm.levelOne_weight_two_rank_zero.
A quadratic twist of E also has CM, so the same argument shows it is not semistable.
Compare with the hypotheses of the BSD.6 and BSD.7 nodes; for 32a2 the absence of an odd-degree rational isogeny makes E[p] irreducible at every odd p.
acceptance: The automorphism (x, y) ↦ (−x, iy) of y² = x³ − x over ℚ(i) squares to [−1] (parent node fixture-32-cm-additive).
A CM curve can satisfy a BSD.7 branch: if E has a rational p-isogeny at a good odd p (as some CM curves do), the Keller–Yin hypotheses can hold.

sources.match: A CM curve and a nonsemistable curve are among the tests, and each source's side conditions are checked before its theorem is applied.
Modular forms of weight two and level one are zero.
The class of 32a2 consists of curves linked by isogenies of degree 2 and 4 (comparison data, not a proof).

nodes.title: No named branch reaches the prime 2
nodes.statement: Each of the seven named prime-part branches (five in BSD.6, two in BSD.7) requires p ≥ 3. Hence, for every E/ℚ with analyticRank E ≤ 1, PrimePartFormula E h 2 can come only from an exact dyadic computation (BSD.8/exceptional-prime-part-adapter) or from a proof that bsdDefect E = 1. By dyadic-gate, PrimePartFormula at every odd prime does not imply the full formula. The rank and Ш endpoints are unaffected: an unproved dyadic part blocks only the full-formula endpoint.
hypotheses: E/ℚ elliptic with analyticRank E ≤ 1.
proofSteps: Read p ≥ 3 (or p > 3, p ≥ 5) from the hypotheses of the seven branch nodes.
Combine with BSD.8/source-qualified-prime-part-dispatch, whose only remaining case is the exceptional-prime adapter, and with dyadic-gate.
acceptance: 11a3 (good at 2), 37a1 (good at 2) and 32a2 (additive at 2) all need a separate dyadic input for the full formula.
The public rank and Ш endpoints have no dyadic hypothesis.

sources.locator: BSD.9, last sentence of the second paragraph
sources.match: An unproved residual 2-part prevents full-formula assembly while leaving rank equality and finite Sha unaffected.

nodes.title: Odd primary Sha vanishing from the Heegner index
nodes.statement: Let E/ℚ be elliptic of conductor N with a fixed modular parametrisation, K imaginary quadratic with D_K ∉ {−3, −4} and every prime dividing N split in K, y_K ∈ E(K) the Heegner point (HE.1), of infinite order, and I_K = [E(K) : ℤy_K]. Let ℓ be an odd prime with ℓ ∤ I_K. (a) If E has no CM and Gal(ℚ(E[ℓ])/ℚ) ≅ GL₂(𝔽_ℓ), then Ш(E/K)[ℓ] = 0. (b) In general, if ℓ ∈ B(E) (the odd primes not dividing the discriminant of End_ℚ̄(E) at which the ℓ-adic image is as large as possible, HE.7), then v_ℓ(#Ш(E/K)) ≤ 2·v_ℓ(I_K) = 0. In either case Ш(E/K)[ℓ^∞] = 0, hence Ш(E/ℚ)[ℓ^∞] = 0 and Ш(E^K/ℚ)[ℓ^∞] = 0.
hypotheses: The classical Heegner hypotheses of HE.7/classical-full-sha-finiteness; y_K non-torsion; ℓ odd with ℓ ∤ I_K.
(a) needs no CM and surjective mod-ℓ image; (b) needs ℓ ∈ B(E).
proofSteps: ℓ ∤ I_K implies y_K ∉ ℓE(K): if y_K = ℓQ then Q has order ℓ in E(K)/ℤy_K, because y_K has infinite order.
(a) HE.6/gross-clean-mod-p-descent: Sel_ℓ(E/K) is generated by the Kummer image of y_K, so Ш(E/K)[ℓ] = 0.
(b) HE.7/classical-square-index-error-bound: #Ш(E/K) divides d_E·I_K² with v_ℓ(d_E) = 0 for ℓ ∈ B(E).
A torsion ℓ-primary group with no element of order ℓ is zero; BSD.1/odd-selmer-sha-decomposition splits Ш(E/K)[ℓ^∞] as Ш(E/ℚ)[ℓ^∞] ⊕ Ш(E^K/ℚ)[ℓ^∞].
acceptance: If ℓ | I_K the theorem gives nothing at ℓ: the index bound is only an upper bound (Gross Conjecture 1.2 is not used).
The prime 2 is excluded: the 2-primary part needs a separate argument (a 2-descent or the comparison BSD.1/two-primary-comparison).

sources.match: Kolyvagin's bound of #Ш(E/K) by an exceptional integer times I_K², and the clean statement that Ш(E/K) has no ℓ-torsion when the mod-ℓ image is GL₂ and ℓ does not divide y_K.
Whole-Sha conclusions need a proved annihilator; here the annihilator is a power of 2 at the primes covered.

nodes.title: Sha of the curve X₀(37)/w₃₇ from a Heegner point of index one
nodes.statement: Let E: y² + y = x³ − x (37a1, the quotient X₀(37)/w₃₇) and P = (0, 0). Assume: (h1) E(ℚ) = ℤP; (h2) there is an imaginary quadratic K with D_K ∉ {−3, −4} in which 37 splits whose Heegner index I_K = [E(K) : ℤy_K] is a power of 2 (for instance y_K = ±P with [E(K) : E(ℚ)] a power of 2; Gross writes y_K = m_K·P and I_K = ±m_K); (h3) Gal(ℚ(E[ℓ])/ℚ) ≅ GL₂(𝔽_ℓ) for ℓ = 3, 5, 7; (h4) Ш(E/ℚ)[2] = 0. Then Ш(E/ℚ) = 0. If in addition E(ℚ)_tors = 0, c₃₇ = 1 and analyticRank E = 1, then bsdDefect E = L′(E,1)/(Ω_E·ĥ_x(P)), and the full formula for E is the single real identity L′(E,1) = Ω_E·ĥ_x(P), with ĥ_x the x-height canonical height.
hypotheses: The four hypotheses (h1)–(h4) are supplied data, not computations of this roadmap; Gross reports (h1) and that y_K ∈ E(ℚ) for this curve.
For ℓ ≥ 11 the mod-ℓ image is GL₂(𝔽_ℓ) because E is semistable (Mazur's theorem, quoted by Gross p.237); (h3) covers the remaining odd primes.
proofSteps: Every odd ℓ satisfies ℓ ∤ I_K by (h2); E has no CM (j = 110592/37 ∉ ℤ); odd-sha-from-heegner-index (a) gives Ш(E/ℚ)[ℓ^∞] = 0 for every odd ℓ.
From (h4), the 2-primary part is zero: a nonzero element of a 2-primary torsion group has a multiple of order 2.
With (h1), Reg_BSD(E/ℚ) = ĥ_x(P) (GZ.0/bsd-regulator); substitute #Ш = 1, #tors = 1 and c₃₇ = 1 in BSD.5's defect.
acceptance: Gross records c = 1 and m₃₇ = 1 for this curve, so his Conjecture 1.2 predicts #Ш(E/K) = I_K²; Kolyvagin's refinement (t_{E/K} a power of 2, equal to 1 when I_K is odd) is reported there and is not used here.
If y_K = ±3P instead, the theorem gives nothing at ℓ = 3.

sources.locator: Example after Theorem 1.3, p.236, and its continuation on p.237
sources.match: For X₀(37)/w₃₇ with the degree-two parametrisation, c = 1 and m₃₇ = 1; y_K lies in E(ℚ), which is infinite cyclic generated by (0,0); writing y_K = m_K·P gives I_K = ±m_K.

nodes.title: Ranks and finite Sha of the three test curves from analytic data
nodes.statement: Let E₁₁: y² + y = x³ − x² (11a3), E₃₇: y² + y = x³ − x (37a1) and E₃₂: y² = x³ − x (32a2, the parent's fixture32). Assume their conductors are 11, 37, 32 and their root numbers +1, −1, +1, and assume for some M ≥ 1 the finite-sum inequalities |S₀(M)| > T₀(M), |S₁(M)| > T₁(M), |S₀(M)| > T₀(M) of explicit-nonvanishing-criterion respectively (or directly L(E₁₁,1) > 0, L′(E₃₇,1) > 0, L(E₃₂,1) > 0). Then the analytic ranks are 0, 1, 0, the ranks of the Mordell–Weil groups are 0, 1, 0, and each Ш(E/ℚ) is finite. For the two semistable curves the root numbers follow from a₁₁(E₁₁) = 1 (split) and a₃₇(E₃₇) = −1 (nonsplit) by the local formula of BSD.0; for E₃₂ the sign is a supplied datum.

BSD.0's rootNumber_eq_prod_local: for prime conductor ℓ with multiplicative reduction the sign is a_ℓ.
acceptance: M = 5 suffices for all three numerically (values listed in explicit-nonvanishing-criterion).
An interval containing 0, or root number −1 without a nonzero derivative, establishes neither rank.

nodes.title: The 5-part on 11a3 through Keller–Yin

With the additional data L(E₁₁,1)/Ω = 1/25 (exact-rank-zero-quotient), #E₁₁(ℚ)_tors = 5 and c₁₁ = 1, the formula gives v₅(#Ш(E₁₁/ℚ)) = 0, i.e. Ш(E₁₁/ℚ)[5^∞] = 0.

nodes.title: Ш = 0 for the three test curves under explicit hypotheses
nodes.statement: Under the following supplied hypotheses, #Ш(E/ℚ) = 1 for the three curves. E₃₇: (h1)–(h4) of gross-37a-sha-vanishing. E₁₁: the data of conditional-eisenstein-five (giving the 5-part); a Heegner field K for E₁₁ whose Heegner point has index I_K prime to every odd ℓ ≠ 5; surjective mod-ℓ image for the odd ℓ ≠ 5 (for ℓ ≥ 11 Mazur's theorem, E₁₁ being semistable); and Ш(E₁₁/ℚ)[2] = 0. E₃₂ (CM by ℤ[i]): a Heegner field K (2 split, D_K ≡ 1 mod 8) whose Heegner index is a power of 2; every odd ℓ in B(E₃₂); and Ш(E₃₂/ℚ)[2] = 0. The analytic hypotheses of conditional-fixture-ranks and these arithmetic hypotheses are distinct inputs: neither implies the other.

E₁₁ at 5: conditional-eisenstein-five. At odd ℓ ≠ 5: odd-sha-from-heegner-index (a) for E₁₁ (5 is excluded from (a) because E₁₁[5] is reducible). At 2: the descent hypothesis.
E₃₂ at odd ℓ: odd-sha-from-heegner-index (b), since E₃₂ has CM. At 2: the descent hypothesis.

nodes.title: The full formula for the three test curves under explicit data
nodes.statement: Assume for E₁₁, E₃₇, E₃₂: rational leading quotients L*/(Ω Reg_BSD) = 1/25, 1, 1/8; torsion orders 5, 1, 4; Tamagawa products 1, 1, 2; #Ш = 1, 1, 1 (conditional-sha-vanishing-fixtures); full real Néron periods; regulators 1, ĥ_x(P), 1 (P the saturated generator of E₃₇(ℚ)). Then bsdDefect = (1/25)·25/1 = 1, 1·1/1 = 1 and (1/8)·16/2 = 1, so PrimeValuationCertificate.ofAllPrimes applies and public-full-endpoint gives the full formula for each curve. The quotient data may be supplied by exact-rank-zero-quotient (rank zero) and by an exact value of L′(E₃₇,1)/(Ω ĥ_x(P)).

In rank zero the regulator is the empty determinant 1 (Tau Ceti regulator_eq_one_of_finrank_eq_zero and GZ.0/bsd-regulator).

decisions.detail: The maintainer's decision of 2026-10-16 (research/blueprint/upstream/drops.json; FIX-PKG-RankZeroOneBSD~adv2 instructions) drops ComputationalNumberTheory CN.4 and makes the explicit modular-curve and 32a2 data hypotheses of the final theorems. The parent's remaining item 'supply/replay all stated rigorous central-value enclosures and finite arithmetic, local, period, saturation and whole-Sha certificates' is therefore read as: plan the general theorems those replays would use, and restate the applications with the data as hypotheses.
E₁ = Γ(0, ·) is imported from QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.3/upper-incomplete-gamma, which plans the upper incomplete gamma for every real s; no second carrier is defined here.
Gross reports that for X₀(37)/w₃₇ Kolyvagin shows t_{E/K} = 1 when I_K is odd; Kolyvagin's paper was not read, so the 2-primary part is a stated descent hypothesis instead.
